intro.title: About this tool
intro.body: This tool compares a page's raw HTML against what a crawler can actually read, then builds a list of actionable findings — not a single score. Search ranking depends on many other factors (content relevance, backlinks, domain authority, and more) that can't be measured from one URL, so this tool focuses on technical hygiene instead of promising a search position.

usage.title: How to use it
steps: Enter the URL of the page you want to check, then click Analyze.
Pick which user-agent to crawl as: Googlebot or Generic bot (full explanation below).
On success, you'll see a summary of findings by severity, the raw facts found (title, description, canonical, etc), and a full list of findings with why each matters and how to fix it.
If the page couldn't be fetched or was blocked, a single explanation banner appears instead of a findings list — see "When you see a banner" below.

userAgent.title: Googlebot vs Generic bot

googlebot.title: Googlebot
googlebot.body: Mimics Googlebot: sends Googlebot's own User-Agent header, and is matched against the site's Googlebot-specific robots.txt group (if one exists). This answers "can Google crawl this page?" — the question most people actually want answered.

generic.title: Generic bot
generic.body: Uses this tool's own bot identity, matched against the generic group (User-agent: *) in robots.txt. This answers "what can a generic crawler, with no special treatment, see?" — useful when a site's robots.txt treats Googlebot differently from everyone else.

userAgent.note: Results can differ by user-agent, since robots.txt can have different rules per user-agent. Important note: many large sites verify Googlebot's identity via reverse DNS / Google's real IP ranges, not just the User-Agent header — so even with Googlebot selected, a site like LinkedIn can still reject the request. That isn't a bug; that's their security working as designed.

outcomes.title: When you see a banner instead of a findings list
outcomes.intro: This tool deliberately doesn't guess when a page couldn't be fetched. Rather than report "title not found" when the page was never actually read, it shows a single banner explaining why content checks were skipped entirely — not treated as failed, just never checked.

items.title: robots.txt disallows it
items.body: The site's robots.txt disallows this path for the user-agent you selected. The tool didn't proceed with fetching the page, out of respect for that rule. Try switching user-agent — results can differ if the site has separate rule groups per user-agent.

items.title: Server blocked it (anti-bot)
items.body: The server responded with a status commonly used to reject automated requests (e.g. 403, 429, or LinkedIn's own 999), not the real page. This usually means the site has an anti-scraping system, not that the page has an SEO problem.

items.title: Other HTTP error
items.body: The page responded with a non-2xx status that isn't an anti-bot signal (e.g. 404 or 500). Worth checking directly whether the page is genuinely broken.

items.title: Too many redirects
items.body: The URL redirected repeatedly without ever reaching a final page. There may be a redirect loop worth fixing.

items.title: Timeout / connection failed
items.body: The server didn't respond in a reasonable time, or the connection failed (e.g. an SSL error or connection refused).

items.title: Domain not found
items.body: The domain name couldn't be resolved. Double-check the URL is correct and the domain is still active.

limits.title: Audit limits
limits.body: To prevent abuse, the number of audits per IP address is limited over a given time window. If you hit the limit, you'll see a message asking you to try again later.

seoDevelopment.title: SEO Development: how the expected output is built
seoDevelopment.intro: The SEO Development page takes a /products path plus a mocked listing response (total products, out-of-stock count, lowest price, top brands) and works out what the page should serve. The rules below run top to bottom; the first one that decides something wins. The generated title and description are always Indonesian, since they're the site's own content.

flow.title: 1. Validate the path
flow.body: The path must start with / and with /products. Anything else shows an error and no result.

flow.title: 2. Search goes first
flow.body: If there's a ?search= query, the page is a search result: canonical is /products, robots is "-" (follows canonical), no internal links, and the title has no length limit. Nothing below applies.

flow.title: 3. Read the path
flow.body: Segments after /products are read as /products/{category}/{vehicle}/{brand}. The first segment is the category; the next ones are classified by the known slug lists (vehicle: mobil, motor; brands: gs-astra, incoe, …). Unknown segments are ignored with a note, more than 3 segments are cut off, and brand-before-vehicle is flagged as the wrong order.

flow.title: 4. Fold query filters in
flow.body: ?category=, ?vehicle= and ?brand= are merged with the path. A category from the query only counts when the path has none. Other params (utm, etc.) are ignored.

flow.title: 5. Pick the canonical
flow.body: The canonical is the one official URL for that combination: /products/{category}/{vehicle}/{brand}, or /products?brand=… / /products?vehicle=… when there's no category. ?page=N is kept from page 2 onward; sort and page=1 are dropped. A filter with several values (brand=a,b), or brand + vehicle without a category, has no PLP: robots noindex, canonical to the nearest real PLP.

flow.title: 6. Decide index / noindex
flow.body: Only when the canonical equals the typed path (self). It's index when total products ≥ the minimum (default 3) and the in-stock share ≥ the minimum (default 50%), otherwise noindex. When the canonical points elsewhere the URL is a variant and robots is "-": no robots tag of its own, it follows the canonical. Follow is always on.

flow.title: 7. Internal links
flow.body: true only for leveling pages (there's a category) or when a brand filter is present. /products, vehicle-only pages and search get false.

flow.title: 8. Build the title
flow.body: The template is chosen from the canonical entities (table below). From page 2 on, " Halaman N" goes before " | Astra Otopart". If the title is longer than the limit (default 60), "Berkualitas" is removed first, then "Jual". Search titles are exempt.

flow.title: 9. Build the description
flow.body: One of six templates (table below), also chosen from the canonical entities. The Vehicle and Category + Brand templates show the in-stock count rounded down to 20+, 50+, 100+, 150+, then every 50; with 20 or fewer in stock the number is left out. From page 2 on, " (Halaman N)" is appended.

seoDevelopment.configNote: Thresholds come from server env vars, read per request (restart, no rebuild): SEO_DEV_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH (default 60), SEO_DEV_MIN_PRODUCTS (default 3), SEO_DEV_MIN_IN_STOCK_PERCENT (default 50).

notes.invalidPage: page={value} is invalid, treated as page 1.
notes.unknownSort: sort={value} isn't a known sort option.
notes.search: Search query present: canonical points to /products and the title length limit doesn't apply.
notes.tooManySegments: More than 3 segments after /products; the rest are ignored.
notes.unknownCategory: Category "{slug}" is unknown; in production this should ideally be a 404.
notes.wrongOrder: Segment order is wrong (should be category/vehicle/brand); ideally a 308 redirect.
notes.unknownSegment: Segment "{slug}" isn't a known vehicle or brand; ignored.
notes.categoryQueryIgnored: The category query is ignored because the path already has a category.
notes.categoryQueryPromoted: category={slug} moves into the path as /products/{slug}.
notes.multiValue: A filter with more than one value isn't a PLP: noindex, canonical to the nearest PLP.
notes.comboWithoutCategory: Brand + vehicle without a category isn't a PLP: noindex, canonical to /products.
notes.sortVariant: Sort doesn't create a new page; canonical drops it.
notes.pageOneVariant: page=1 is the first page; canonical drops it.
notes.variant: This URL is a variant; its index status follows the canonical.
notes.titleStillLong: Title is still {length} characters after removing every optional word.
